_comment: The regression question set. Keep it fixed: an experiment is only useful
if two runs asked the same things, so change this file deliberately and
expect scores before and after not to be comparable when you do.
HARDENED 2026-07-22: the Linear Algebra 'answerable' entries were replaced
with specific, proof-level questions built and verified by scripts/build_eval_set.py
(generate from a real chunk -> a second model confirms it is answerable ONLY
from that passage -> confirm the chunk is retrievable). The old set was generic
definitions the book covers redundantly, so top_k=3 and top_k=8 scored the same;
these need a specific page, so retrieval changes finally register. Baselines from
before this date are NOT comparable. One easy control ('What is a vector?') is kept
as a high-score anchor.
`gold_page` (answerable-hard only) is the page the question was written from, for
gold-aware retrieval checks; graders don't read it. `difficulty` flows into the
experiment row metadata, so scores can be sliced easy vs medium on the platform.
`subject` matches a subject name in storage/subjects.json (case-insensitive).
A question whose subject isn't present is skipped and reported.
Aim for a spread the graders can actually separate:
- answerable      the books cover it; expect high scores across the board
- partial         the books cover part of it; completeness should drop
- out-of-corpus   the books don't cover it; the tutor must refuse, which
is a PASS for groundedness and a low context relevance
`mode` is "qa" when absent. Lecture entries grade the same way but retrieve
a continuous run of the book, so their context relevance is expected to be
lower: neighbours are pulled in for continuity, not because they match.
